title: Dedicated tiers + Throughput SLO docs (customer-facing overview, FAQ, examples)
author: Elliot Price
release_notes: Adds customer-facing Dedicated tier overview and Throughput SLO explanation, including measurement details, exclusions, remedies pointer, and FAQ. Updates docs IA/nav to surface Dedicated tiers and SLO content.
body: Summary: This PR adds customer-facing documentation for Redwood Dedicated tiers (Standard / Plus / Premium) and a clear, contract-aligned explanation of the Dedicated Throughput SLO: what we guarantee, how we measure it, what conditions apply, and what customers can do if they believe they are below commitment. The goal is to reduce sales/support ambiguity and set correct expectations around committed throughput vs burst, tier entitlements, and exclusions (e.g., customer-side throttling, unsupported models/versions, cold start/warmup windows). Motivation: We have repeated questions in sales calls and support tickets about “throughput guarantees in writing,” plus confusion around burst usage vs committed capacity. This content is intended to match the current PRD direction and SRE metric semantics while being readable to engineering buyers. Scope: (1) Dedicated tiers overview (who each tier is for, entitlements, what is/isn’t guaranteed); (2) Dedicated Throughput SLO page with definition, measurement window, eligible endpoints, and exclusions; (3) FAQ addressing common objections (streaming, batching/caching, multi-model deployments, model pinning, regional capacity, and how to size); (4) examples with simple numbers and diagrams for “committed vs burst” and “how to interpret tokens/sec charts”; (5) glossary and cross-links to Console dashboards and support escalation entry points. Out of scope: The actual contract language and pricing tables; those remain in order forms/MSA and sales enablement materials. Implementation notes: The SLO page is written to avoid over-specifying implementation details that may change (kernel selection, batching algorithms), but it does define the canonical measurement at a level customers can audit: throughput is computed from server-side token accounting for successful generation tokens over a rolling window, attributed per Dedicated deployment, excluding customer-requested throttling and known non-serving periods (maintenance windows and control-plane initiated deploy events). We also explicitly call out that model choice and max context affect achievable performance and that commitments apply to supported model/version combinations listed for the deployment. The streaming section includes a note on how token counting is handled for streaming responses (tokens count as generated as they are emitted) to preempt confusion from client-side clocks. Docs added/updated: - docs/dedicated/overview.md (new) - docs/dedicated/tiers.md (new) - docs/dedicated/throughput-slo.md (new) - docs/dedicated/throughput-slo-faq.md (new) - docs/dedicated/throughput-slo-examples.md (new) - docs/glossary.md (update: Dedicated-specific terms) - docs/support/escalations.md (update: Dedicated SLO routing entry) - site/nav.yml (update) - redirects.yml (update) Key customer-facing wording (excerpt): “Dedicated Throughput SLO: For eligible requests served by your Dedicated deployment, Redwood commits that sustained throughput will meet or exceed your purchased throughput floor when measured over a rolling 30-minute window, excluding periods where requests are not eligible (e.g., customer-side throttling, unsupported models/versions, warmup after a deployment event, or client disconnects). If you believe your deployment is below the purchased throughput floor, contact Support with your deployment ID and the timeframe; Redwood will investigate using server-side metrics and provide remediation per your Dedicated terms.” FAQ highlights: - What is committed throughput vs burst? - How is throughput measured for streaming? - Do retries count? (no; only successfully generated tokens) - What happens if we change models or context length? (commitments apply to supported profiles; re-sizing may be required) - What if we use multiple models in one deployment? (commitment is per-deployment; we document recommended patterns and advise separate deployments for distinct model classes when SLOs matter) - How do we verify? (Console SLO widget / metrics, and how to open an escalation) Screenshots/diagrams: This PR includes lightweight SVG diagrams (no product screenshots) to avoid drift; the Console references link to the “Dedicated monitoring” section which is updated separately by Console teams. Checklist: - [x] Align terminology with PM-503 (tier names, “throughput floor,” “burst”) - [x] Reviewed exclusions with SRE (measurement + window) - [x] Legal review for “do not over-promise” wording; references contract for remedies - [x] Linkcheck + build passes - [x] Added redirects for old internal-only Dedicated doc URLs Review guidance: Please focus on (a) correctness of SLO semantics/exclusions, (b) whether the tier page is consistent with current packaging guidance, and (c) whether any phrasing reads like a contractual promise beyond the intended scope.

review_conversation: Lauren Bishop: Tier table reads well. Please avoid implying Plus includes cross-region failover by default; that’s Premium-only per current packaging. Also add a one-liner that “burst is not guaranteed” and is best-effort subject to pool availability.
Elliot Price (author): Updated tiers.md to remove “regional failover” language from Plus and added an explicit “Burst is best-effort, not guaranteed” note in both tiers.md and the FAQ.

Sean Gallagher: SLO page is close. Two tweaks: (1) Don’t say “measured over 30 minutes” without clarifying rolling window vs calendar window; (2) exclusions should include customer-side 429s (client hitting customer-configured rate limits) and client disconnects for streaming.

Elliot Price (author): Clarified “rolling 30-minute window” in the definition and added explicit exclusions for customer-configured throttling / 429s and client disconnects. Also added a sentence that the source of truth is server-side metrics.

Sofia Mendes: Please remove “provide remediation” phrasing; link to “remedies are defined in your Dedicated Order Form / Service Terms” instead. Also suggest avoiding “commits that sustained throughput will meet or exceed” and using “target”/“service level objective” unless the customer has SLO terms in writing.

Elliot Price (author): Updated wording to “Throughput SLO (Service Level Objective)” and added “If your order form includes a throughput commitment…” qualifier. Replaced “remediation” with “investigate and respond per your terms.”

Soojin Lee: Marketing nit: add a short “Choosing a tier” section with 3 bullets (cost sensitivity vs predictability vs support) and a small callout that Dedicated is for predictable throughput vs Hosted for flexibility.
Elliot Price (author): Added “Choosing a tier” section on tiers.md and a link to the Hosted vs Dedicated comparison page.
Rachel Kim: From CS perspective, can we add a “What to send Support” checklist (deployment_id, region, model, timeframe, example request IDs) to reduce back-and-forth?
Elliot Price (author): Added a checklist at the bottom of throughput-slo.md and mirrored it in support/escalations.md.
